When must the buckling of a micropile be checked separately?
if the undrained shear strength of the soil is c<sub>u</sub> < 10 kPa
if the pile is longer than 10 m
if the groundwater is above the pile head
Because of the small diameter, in very soft soil (c<sub>u</sub> < 10 kPa) the lateral support of the soil is small – then buckling can become governing.
What happens when a hollow-bar grouted micropile (e.g. Ischebeck Titan) is installed?
a hollow bar with a sacrificial drill bit is drilled down with continuous grouting
a precast steel tube is driven down, then pulled out
the bore is supported with bentonite slurry, then concreted through a tremie pipe
the bar is pulled out and its place filled with gravel
The bar is at the same time the drill rod, the grouting pipe and the permanent core. A cement body of 20–50 mm forms around it, and outside that a permeated soil sleeve of 30–80 mm.
At what pressure is the binder injected into the soil in jet grouting?
The binder is jetted through the 2–5 mm nozzles at a pressure of 400–600 bar. 5–6 bar is the pressure of the air shroud in the double jet with air.
With the same technology, in which soil is the largest jet column obtained?
The diameter depends on the permeability of the soil: at most 60–70 cm in clay, up to 150–200 cm in gravel.
What is the essence of the double jet with air?
the cement jet is surrounded by an air shroud at 5–6 bar, so the range increases
two cement jets fire against each other
first they drill with air, then grout with cement
the air sucks out the returning spoil
The air shroud reduces the “braking” of the jet in the soil, so a larger column diameter can be achieved.
What is the danger if the returning spoil cannot escape to the surface during grouting?
hydraulic fracturing, heave of the surface and the building
the jet column becomes too thin
the drill rod freezes in
The free outflow of the excess material must be watched all the time – otherwise the pressure builds up in the soil.
How is a jet panel made?
pulled up without rotation, with two opposite nozzles
with slower rotation but higher pressure
by grouting two adjacent columns at once
by horizontal drilling from the side of the pit
If the rod is not rotated, the two nozzles only “sweep” the soil in one plane: the result is a thin, planar element – joined in a V shape, a watertight curtain wall.
How does deep mixing differ from jet grouting?
the soil is mixed with the binder in place by a rotating, bladed mixing shaft, not by a high-pressure jet
in deep mixing the soil is excavated and mixed at the surface
deep mixing uses no binder
deep mixing only works in rock
The mixing tool does the work, so the size of the element is close to that of the tool.
Which statement is true of the vibro stone column (gravel pile)?
the stone column and the soil between carry the load together – a transition towards ground improvement
it is an independent load-bearing pile standing on its tip
it is a steel tube filled with concrete
it can only be made above the groundwater, in cohesive soil
The gravel column compacted with a vibrating probe stiffens and drains; part of the load goes to the soil, which is why it is also classed as ground improvement.

Jacking

Quiz – precast piles
Why do both the base and the shaft resistance of a driven precast pile increase?
Because the displacement compacts the soil around and below the pile
Because the strength of the concrete increases during driving
Because driving removes the groundwater permanently
Because the surface of the pile is rougher than that of a bored pile
A displacement pile brings up no soil: it pushes it aside and compacts it. For a precast pile this increases both the base and the shaft resistance.
Which layer can a precast reinforced concrete pile not be driven through?
A thin, strongly cemented band
Fine sand below the groundwater
Driving cannot be used in rock, rocky ground, hard (stony) clay, strongly cemented soil and blocky fill – even a thin intercalation can stop the pile.
During driving the set drops almost to zero above the design base depth. What does this mean?
The pile has refused: it has probably hit a hard intercalation
It has reached the bearing stratum, we are done
The hammer energy is too high
The groundwater is floating the pile up
If the pile stops above the design depth, something is in its way. It must not be driven on “by force”: the pile head may be damaged, and the base is not in the planned layer either.
Where is a steel tubular pile advantageous?
Soft, loose soil at the top, a dense granular layer below
If there is rock near the surface
In very hard, stony clay
If the pile has to be made of timber
The tubular pile passes through the soft layer and “stands” in the dense granular layer. For harder layers the H-section is better, because it is easier to drive.
A city-centre infill site with a vibration-sensitive neighbouring building. Which is the riskiest piling technology?
Driving comes with loud noise and strong vibration; near structures it can only be used under strict limits. Bored, screw and micropiles are low in noise and vibration.
In which soil is vibration effective primarily?
In granular soil
In cohesive, hard clay
In rock
In organic, peaty soil
Vibration tuned to the natural frequency of the soil temporarily reduces the resistance to a minimum in granular soil. In cohesive soil this effect is small because of cohesion.
When vibrating with jetting, when must jetting be stopped?
1–2 m before reaching the pile tip (final base depth)
Already after the top 1–2 m
Only when the final base depth is reached
Never, jetting can continue throughout
Jetting must be stopped 1–2 m before the final base depth so that the soil below the base does not loosen. The base can be grouted through the pipes afterwards.
